title: Plural with final a/ä → ia/iä
summary: For these selected words, replace final a/ä with ia/iä: koira (“dog”) → koiria.
objectives: Form the plural partitive in this bounded word family.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A case is a word form used for a grammatical job. The dictionary form is the form used to look up a word. The partitive has several uses; it does not always mean “some”. Here you practise forming the word, so no sentence construction is required.

For the selected koira-type words with o or u in the first syllable, replace final -a with -ia. For the selected -ä words, replace final -ä with -iä. In both groups the original final vowel disappears before plural i. Keep the strong consonants. Learn the family with the word; similar spelling alone does not identify every plural pattern.
keyPoints: Learn each word with its pattern; a similar final letter does not guarantee the same stem.

steps: The word’s meaning stays connected to “dog”; its plural case form changes its grammatical use.

commonMistakes: Do not retain a/ä before plural i.
Do not apply the -oja pattern to koira.
Keep the strong consonants in kukkia and pöytiä.
